technical_and_design_decisions: Target Java 17+ and Spring Framework 6.x / Spring Boot baseline, consistent with the stated Spring version requirement.

Build the increment on the existing Spring XD module/streaming infrastructure (modules communicating over the message bus with a Kafka binder); each feature is delivered as an extension to that platform rather than a standalone system.

U1: Implement a Spring Data repository adapter backed by a local off-heap key-value state store (Chronicle Map style), with state recovery and change capture via a compacted Kafka changelog topic; writes go to the local store and are mirrored to the changelog for fault tolerance.

U2: Commit/flush consumer offsets only after successful acknowledgement callbacks from the Kafka module-producer, using batched, throttled commits of the highest contiguous acknowledged offset to bound reprocessing.

U3: Trigger flush/checkpoint of the local state store only after successful producer acknowledgements so that persisted state and emitted output stay consistent (at-least-once with idempotent recovery).

U4: Implement the CoAP source module with the Eclipse Californium library, exposing a CoAP server endpoint that converts incoming CoAP payloads into module messages; expose endpoint, port, and content-format options as module properties.
U5: Document the properties file as the deployment manifest in the reference documentation (AsciiDoc), covering every property, defaults, and examples.
U6: Support Kerberos-secured HDFS for Sqoop job modules via principal/keytab configuration using Hadoop UserGroupInformation and delegation token acquisition before job submission.
U7: Implement the Diego receptor Java client as a typed REST client (Spring RestTemplate) with JSON model classes for DesiredLRP/ActualLRP/Task operations, plus authentication and error mapping.

U8: Provide a Boot-based ModuleRunner that bootstraps modules as plain Spring Boot apps for container-managed environments (no xd-container), and complete the remaining deployment properties handling (module counts, deployment criteria, and related metadata).
Testing strategy: JUnit unit tests per component plus integration tests using embedded Kafka, a mock CoAP client, a Kerberos-enabled test HDFS cluster, and a stubbed receptor API.
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are pure effort in workdays (8 hours/day), excluding elapsed-time effects such as waiting on environments or reviewers.
The existing Spring XD/streaming codebase, build system (Gradle/Maven), and CI pipeline are already in place and working; only incremental build configuration is needed.
Kafka brokers, a Kerberos KDC with a secured HDFS cluster, and a Diego/receptor test environment (or suitable stubs) are available for integration testing.
The Diego receptor REST API contract is documented and stable, so no reverse engineering is required.
No user interface work is required; all features are libraries, modules, runners, and documentation.
Each activity estimate includes implementation plus its own debugging; dedicated unit and integration testing activities are broken out separately.
Code review effort is limited to self-review and rework by the single developer, since all development work is performed personally.
The CoAP module requires server-side (consumer) functionality only; no CoAP client/sink module is in scope.
Requirements changes are out of scope; minor clarification of story details is handled through the design decisions listed.

activities.activity_name: U4 implementation: CoAP endpoint and message conversion
activities.activity_description: Implement the CoAP server endpoint using Eclipse Californium, converting received CoAP payloads into module messages.

activities.activity_name: U4 module options and properties metadata
activities.activity_description: Define and wire module properties (port, resources, content formats) and their configuration metadata.

activities.activity_name: U4 unit tests
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for resource handlers, payload conversion, and option binding.

activities.activity_name: U4 integration tests with CoAP client
activities.activity_description: Integration tests exercising the module end-to-end with a CoAP client over UDP.

activities.activity_name: U5 documentation: properties file as deployment manifest
activities.activity_description: Write reference documentation describing the properties file used as deployment manifest: all properties, defaults, semantics, and configuration examples.

activities.activity_name: U6 design: Kerberos support for Sqoop job modules
activities.activity_description: Design authentication approach (principal/keytab, credential refresh, delegation tokens) for running Sqoop jobs against a secured HDFS cluster.

activities.activity_name: U6 implementation: secure HDFS/Sqoop configuration
activities.activity_description: Implement Kerberos login via UserGroupInformation, keytab handling, and delegation token acquisition prior to Sqoop job submission.

activities.activity_name: U6 unit tests
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for security configuration parsing and authentication logic (mocked Hadoop security classes).

activities.activity_name: U6 integration tests on secured HDFS cluster
activities.activity_description: Set up/verify a Kerberos-enabled test cluster and run Sqoop jobs end-to-end against secured HDFS, including negative authorization cases.

activities.activity_name: U7 design: Java receptor client API and models
activities.activity_description: Design the Java client facade, JSON model classes (DesiredLRP, ActualLRP, Task), and exception hierarchy for the Diego receptor REST API.

activities.activity_name: U7 implementation: receptor REST client operations
activities.activity_description: Implement the REST client covering LRP and task lifecycle operations against the receptor endpoints.

activities.activity_name: U7 implementation: authentication and error handling
activities.activity_description: Implement client authentication, response error mapping, and retry/timeout behavior.

activities.activity_name: U7 unit tests with mock server
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for all client operations, serialization, and error paths using a stubbed HTTP server.

activities.activity_name: U7 integration tests
activities.activity_description: Integration tests of the client against a running (or faithfully stubbed) Diego receptor API.

activities.activity_name: U8 design: Boot-based ModuleRunner
activities.activity_description: Design a Spring Boot-based ModuleRunner that launches modules standalone for container-managed environments without xd-container.

activities.activity_name: U8 implementation: ModuleRunner
activities.activity_description: Implement the Boot-based runner: module context bootstrapping, message bus binding, and lifecycle management.

activities.activity_name: U8 implementation: remaining deployment properties work
activities.activity_description: Complete the remaining deployment properties support (module counts, deployment criteria, and related metadata handling) per the story scope.

activities.activity_name: U8 unit tests
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for runner bootstrapping and deployment property resolution.

activities.activity_name: U8 integration tests
activities.activity_description: Integration tests deploying and running modules via the Boot-based ModuleRunner in a container-managed style setup.

activities.activity_name: System/end-to-end testing and defect fixing
activities.activity_description: Cross-feature end-to-end testing of the increment (streaming with state flush/offset flush, CoAP ingestion, secure Sqoop jobs, receptor client, ModuleRunner) and fixing defects found.

activities.activity_name: Code self-review and rework
activities.activity_description: Review all new code for consistency with project conventions, refactor, and address findings.

activities.activity_name: Release packaging and documentation finalization
activities.activity_description: Finalize build artifacts, release notes, and integrate user documentation for the increment.
